items.title: A digitally controlled silicon quantum processing unit
items.summary: A silicon quantum processing unit executes high-fidelity multiqubit circuits, with all time-varying control signals generated by a digitally programmed cryogenic complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor controller and delivered to the low-noise, exchange-only qubit device through a high-density superconducting ribbon cable.

items.title: A global view of human centromere variation and evolution
items.summary: Complete sequencing of more than 2,000 centromeres from diverse humans reveals structures and elevated mutation rates that shape the evolution of these critically important regions.

items.title: Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP
items.summary: In senescent cells, mitochondria-derived acetyl-CoA promotes histone acetylation and increases chromatin accessibility at inflammatory gene loci. Inhibition of SLC25A1 attenuates these effects, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting mitochondrial metabolism and its epigenetic crosstalk to delay age-related functional decline.

items.title: Weight-four parity checks in a spin-shuttling architecture
items.summary: A silicon spin-qubit device comprising a shuttling bus for transporting qubits is used to achieve parity checks up to weight four, highlighting the feasibility and benefits of incorporating shuttling into semiconductor quantum processors.

items.title: Rational design of disordered proteins for sequence–function investigation
items.summary: GOOSE enables the design and testing of thousands of disordered protein region sequences to reveal distinct sequence-to-function relationships.

items.title: In situ structure of the poxvirus portal complex
items.summary: Cryo-electron tomography uncovers the structure of a conserved hexameric ‘portal complex’ that spans the core wall in vaccinia virus, and shows how it is associated with viral functions such as assembly, mRNA release and genome uncoating.

items.title: In situ structures of plant photosystem supercomplexes
items.summary: The cryo‑EM structure of the Oryza sativa photosystem II–light harvesting complex II supercomplex in its native membrane reveals the intact plant photosystem architecture, retaining physiologically relevant proteins and lipids that are otherwise lost during purification.

items.title: Photocatalytic water splitting by 2D polymer with out-of-plane carrier flow
items.summary: A strategy using polymeric carbon nitride crystals induces out-of-plane carrier migration by means of internal electric fields applied on facet-selective nanofilms placed on polymer photocatalysts, increasing the apparent quantum efficiency for overall water splitting.

items.title: Miniaturizing and modifying natural proteins with Raygun
items.summary: Probabilistic sequence encoding from language model embeddings within a generative AI framework enables protein miniaturization, modification and augmentation while maintaining native architecture and functional integrity.

items.title: Fires in Europe are breaking records: here’s what the future holds
items.summary: Countries such as Spain and France can expect fire regimes more like those of California as climate change favours hot, dry conditions, scientists suggest.

items.title: Daily briefing: ‘Raygun’ AI can shrink or supersize proteins
items.summary: The tool can add, remove or swap protein subunits using similar steps to natural evolution. Plus, spin qubits are back in the quantum race and the drugs that could prevent long COVID.

items.title: Diverse bacterial pattern recognition receptors sense the core phage proteome
items.summary: Systematic analysis of prokaryotic STAND NTPases — relatives of animal and plant immune receptors — uncovers diverse antiviral sensors that detect most of the core structural and replicative proteins of bacteriophages.

items.title: Alternating CO<sub>2</sub> and bicycloalkane copolymerization to circular polyesters
items.summary: A simple organic catalyst enables direct alternating copolymerization of CO2 with bicycloalkanes to produce high-performance polyesters that can be selectively depolymerized and recycled in a closed-loop lifecycle.

items.title: Sequential reading of a stepwise-shortened peptide immobilized on nanopore
items.summary: A nanopore-based ‘chop and measure’ method sequences peptides at single-amino-acid resolution by using enzymatic digestion to progressively shorten the N terminus one residue at a time, together with repetitive N-terminus re-reading.

items.title: Enzymatic glycosylation and amidation reshapes polyene bioactivity
items.summary: Pathways to previously undescribed polyenes, including unusual enzymes that introduce more sugars onto polyene scaffolds, are discovered, and their accessibility through clean and efficient fermentation and potential for safe use as antifungal treatments is described.

items.title: Plasmonic metamaterial time crystal
items.summary: A plasmonic metamaterial driven at terahertz frequencies achieves strong, ultrafast temporal modulation and shows a transition to the photonic time crystal regime with reduced plasmonic losses.

items.title: Octahedral-coordinated Co<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub> for water electrolysis in acid
items.summary: A new trigonal-phase Co3O4 manufactured using a vacuum-mediated molten-alkali mechanochemical method is described, demonstrating edge-shared octahedral coordination and achieving lower overpotential than spinel-type Co3O4 in the acidic oxygen evolution reaction, with reduced dissolution of cobalt.

items.title: Over 20,000 precolonial earthworks in the Southwest Amazonia
items.summary: Using canopy-penetrating LiDAR data, the northern part of southwestern Amazonia appears to contain as many earthworks as previously estimated for the whole of Amazonia.

items.title: How smallpox reached the Americas: first genomic evidence points to Europeans
items.summary: Viral sequences from Chilean mummies confirm the disease was introduced from Europe.

items.title: Somatic mutations reveal the ontogeny of microglia in human aging
items.summary: Somatic mutations reveal the ontogeny of microglia in human aging

items.title: The piezochiral effect
items.summary: The piezochiral effect, a new member of the family of strain-responsive functionalities alongside piezoelectricity and piezomagnetism, is introduced, enabling control of chirality through mechanical strain, with future applications in photonics, spintronics, biosensing and quantum information.

items.title: Avalanche-like intercalation and intraparticle correlations in graphite
items.summary: Operando optical microscopy shows avalanche-like lithium deintercalation (intercalation) processes as the dilute stages of graphite are emptied (filled), showing how local disorder governs phase-transition dynamics and ion transport in lithium-ion battery electrodes.

items.title: Perpendicular switching of polarization in layered ferroelectrics
items.summary: Perpendicular switching of the polarization state in the layered ferroelectric Bi4Ti3O12 is demonstrated by means of trilinear coupling, allowing manipulation of the in-plane polarization component with an out-of-plane electric field.

items.title: Earliest siphuncle-bearing cephalopod from the early Cambrian
items.summary: Early Cambrian Eoceras shaanxiense gen. et sp. nov. preserves septa and a segmented tube resembling a primordial siphuncle, extending cephalopod origins and revealing early assembly of chambered shells used for buoyancy regulation.

items.title: Climate benefit and ecological cost trade-offs for ocean iron fertilization
items.summary: A process-rich global biogeochemical model is used to determine the trade-offs between carbon dioxide removal efficiency and ecosystem impacts in ten ocean ocean biomes following ocean iron fertilization.

items.title: Sickle-cell disease linked to prematurely aged stem cells in mice
items.summary: A combination of drugs restores stem-cell function in mouse models of the blood disorder.

items.title: Scientists using LLMs will ‘do more, less well’, modelling study predicts
items.summary: Research suggests that the combination of incentives to publish and the use of large language models will lead to more papers, but they will be less refined.

items.title: Demand for lithium is surging: here’s how to make mining more sustainable
items.summary: Researchers are looking for ways to extract the metal from underground reservoirs that use less water.

items.title: Earthworks spotted in the Amazon hint at huge ancient civilization
items.summary: Discovery of almost 400 structures may help to redefine the true scale of the Aquiry civilization — plus, tiny fossils of the earliest fossil squid ancestor.

items.title: Cretaceous zhelestid mammals are zalambdalestoids
items.summary: New Mongolian fossil evidence shows zhelestids were not placental-like herbivore relatives, but a dental variant within Zalambdalestoidea, with distinctive molars alongside zalambdalestid skull and limb traits.

items.title: ‘A waste of time for all of us’: caught in the crossfire of the peer-review wars
items.summary: Review mills — researchers who write fake referee reports with coercive citation requests — are setting off a war in academic publishing. What happens to those caught in the middle?

items.title: Meat allergy is on the rise — what scientists want to know
items.summary: The allergy is caused by ticks, but researchers have much to learn about it.

items.title: New-deal mortgage programmes benefited white borrowers disproportionately
items.summary: New data on homebuying loan records around the Second World War in the USA, linked to race and immigration status, show that Black borrowers were disproportionally excluded from mortgage programmes.

items.title: Briefing Chat: Orcas smashed a sunfish to bits — researchers aren’t sure why
items.summary: Nature staff discuss a massive survey of insects in the Amazon, and unusual orca behaviour caught on video.

items.title: Was art key to ancient humans' success? The secrets of Hohle Fels cave
items.summary: New discoveries at famous archeological site add to mystery of ancient human culture.

items.title: Plans for nuclear-powered merchant ships must confront risks
items.summary: Vessels propelled by atomic reactors have low emissions but create other hazards that need clear regulations.

items.title: The secret relationships that govern life on Earth
items.summary: Books on parasitism and symbiosis inspire wonder at the strange ways in which species’ lives intertwine.

items.title: How I use statistics and my law degree to fight human-rights abuses
items.summary: Some 50 years after exposing gender discrimination in US academics’ retirement benefits, Mary Gray works as a statistician and social-justice campaigner.

items.title: Why tomorrow’s nanotechnologies need support today
items.summary: The field seems to be on the cusp of big advances, but a concerted effort is needed to realize its true potential.

items.title: The physics of fizz: why some bubbles are louder than others
items.summary: A high-speed camera and underwater microphones help scientists to investigate a puzzle about bubbles.

items.title: The forensic traces that can help catch poachers — July’s best science images
items.summary: The month’s sharpest science shots, selected by Nature’s photo team.

items.title: Job insecurity is chipping away at me and my cohort. Is it us, or the state of the economy?
items.summary: The career market is difficult to navigate — and academic achievements feel like they’re no longer enough, says Daniella Watson.

items.title: Science-backed tips on how to avoid distractions
items.summary: Struggling to stay focused in the lab? Attention researchers offer some advice.

items.title: Daily Briefing: How smallpox reached the Americas
items.summary: Viral sequences from Chilean mummies confirm smallpox was introduced to the Americas from Europe. Plus, the month’s best science images and the changing patterns of Europe’s wildfires.

items.summary: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.
